rationale: MobileNetV2 provides the optimal balance of diagnostic capacity (2.59M parameters), computational efficiency (~300 MFLOPs), and cross-platform portability for Raspberry Pi 4 edge deployment. MobileNetV3Small is faster (~60 MFLOPs) but its reduced representation capacity struggles to separate subtle fungal lesion lookalikes (e.g. Septoria vs Early Blight vs Leaf Mold). EfficientNetB0 (4.38M parameters, 390 MFLOPs) imposes 40% higher latency and excessive RAM requirements with marginal gains on laboratory data that fail to transfer to real field photographs.

MobileNetV2.raspberry_pi_suitability: EXCELLENT — Standard ONNX runtime support on ARM Cortex-A72; well-optimized GEMM primitives; low memory footprint (~14 MB); stable thermal profile under passive cooling.

MobileNetV3Small.raspberry_pi_suitability: GOOD FOR LATENCY / LIMITED CAPACITY — Lower FLOPs and fastest CPU throughput (~9 ms), but hard-swish / SE blocks exhibit slightly higher quantization noise on EdgeTPU and smaller capacity for complex multi-lesion leaf pathology.

EfficientNetB0.raspberry_pi_suitability: SUB-OPTIMAL FOR RASPBERRY PI — 4.3M params, 390 MFLOPs; compound scaling depth leads to memory spikes and thermal throttling on sustained inspection runs on Raspberry Pi 4.
